prompt: For `record Book(Isbn isbn, String title, int year)`, how do you read the title?
hint: The accessors are named after the components.

choices.text: `book.getTitle()`
choices.why: That is the usual name in a hand-written class; a record's accessor has no `get`.

choices.text: `book.title()`
choices.why: Right: one accessor per component, with the component's own name.

choices.text: `book.title`, because the field is public
choices.why: The field is `private final`, as `javap -p` showed.

choices.text: `book.get("title")`
choices.why: Records have no lookup by name; each component has its own method.

prompt: `a` and `b` are two `Book` records built with equal components. `a == b` printed `false` and `a.equals(b)` printed `true`. Why the difference?
hint: `new` ran twice.

choices.text: `==` compares references and the generated `equals` compares components
choices.why: Right: two objects, equal values.

choices.text: `equals` is broken for records whose component is another record
choices.why: `Isbn` is a record too, and its own `equals` compared the values; nothing is broken.

choices.text: The JVM reuses one object for equal records, but `==` ignores that
choices.why: No object was reused: `==` returned `false` precisely because there were two.

prompt: `javap -p Book` showed what the compiler wrote for the record. Which of these were in it? Choose all that apply.
hint: Read the listing from the top.

choices.text: `private final` fields, one per component
choices.why: Yes: `isbn`, `title` and `year`.

choices.text: `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString`
choices.why: Yes, all three, generated from the components.

choices.text: A setter for each component
choices.why: There is none and there can be none; the fields are final.

choices.text: A constructor with no parameters
choices.why: The one constructor takes every component, in order: `Book(Isbn, java.lang.String, int)`.

prompt: A record's header lists its ___, and the compiler builds the fields, the constructor and the accessors from them.
hint: The word section 02 gives the record's declared values.

prompt: You add a component, `String author`, to the `Book` header and recompile. What else must you change for `equals` and `toString` to include it?
hint: Who wrote those methods?

choices.text: Both methods, by hand, and the constructor
choices.why: None of them is yours to edit; they are generated from the header on every compile.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right: the header is the single place the components are named, so nothing can fall out of step.

choices.text: Only `hashCode`, which the compiler cannot generate for strings
choices.why: It generates `hashCode` for any component type.

choices.text: An annotation on the component asking for it to be included
choices.why: Every component is included; there is nothing to ask for.

prompt: In `Isbn`'s compact constructor, `value = value.replace("-", "").strip();` reassigns what?
hint: The compact constructor runs before the fields are assigned.

choices.text: The field `value`, which is final and so cannot be reassigned again
choices.why: The field is assigned once, after the block; this line changes something else.

choices.text: The parameter, whose final value the field then receives
choices.why: Right: the compiler assigns the field from the parameter at the end of the block.

choices.text: The string the caller passed, which now loses its hyphens too
choices.why: Strings are immutable; `replace` returned a new string and the caller's is untouched.

prompt: `new Isbn("978-85-359")` threw `IllegalArgumentException`. What can the rest of the program now assume about every `Isbn` it receives?
hint: A bad one is refused before it exists.

choices.text: Nothing until it calls a `validate()` method
choices.why: There is no such method; the check is in the constructor, which every `Isbn` passed through.

choices.text: That it has hyphens in the usual places
choices.why: The constructor removed the hyphens; it stores thirteen digits.

choices.text: That it holds thirteen characters, with no hyphens or spaces
choices.why: Right: valid by construction, so no method has to check again.

prompt: `new Isbn(" 978-85-359-0277-1 ")` printed `Isbn[value=9788535902771]`. How many characters did the constructor remove?
hint: Four hyphens and two spaces.

prompt: After `titles.add("Iracema")` in `main`, `Shelf` showed two titles and `SafeShelf` one. What made the difference?
hint: What does each record's field point at?

choices.text: `SafeShelf`'s field is `final` and `Shelf`'s is not
choices.why: Both fields are `final`; a record has no other kind.

choices.text: `SafeShelf` copied the list; `Shelf` kept the caller's own
choices.why: Right: `List.copyOf` in the compact constructor cut the link to the caller's list.

choices.text: `Shelf`'s `toString` reads the list again each time and `SafeShelf`'s does not
choices.why: Both `toString` methods read their field; the fields point at different lists.

choices.text: Records copy their components by default, and `Shelf` turned that off
choices.why: Records copy nothing by default; that is why `SafeShelf` had to.

prompt: Which component type needs a copy in the compact constructor for the record to be really immutable?
hint: Which of these can change after it is handed over?

choices.text: `String`
choices.why: Strings are immutable already.

choices.text: `int`
choices.why: A primitive is copied by value; nothing can change it from outside.

choices.text: `List<String>`
choices.why: Right: the field is a final reference to a list that anybody holding it can change.

choices.text: Another record, such as `Isbn`
choices.why: A record whose own components are immutable is immutable too.

prompt: What does `case Book(String title, int pages)` do when `item` is a `Book`?
hint: A pattern does two jobs.

choices.text: Calls `Book`'s constructor with the two values
choices.why: Nothing is built; the existing record is taken apart.

choices.text: Matches, and leaves you to cast `item` to `Book` yourself
choices.why: No cast is needed; that is half of what the pattern does for you.

choices.text: Matches it, and puts its components in two new variables
choices.why: Right: it tests and takes apart in one step.

prompt: Why did `describe` compile with no `default` branch?
hint: What does `sealed` tell the compiler?

choices.text: `permits` lists every possible `Item`, and each has a case
choices.why: Right: the compiler checked the cases against a complete list.

choices.text: Because a switch over records never needs `default`
choices.why: Over a type that is not sealed it does; the records alone do not make the list complete.

choices.text: Because the guarded case catches whatever the others miss
choices.why: A guard narrows a case; it cannot catch types the case does not name.

choices.text: Because `describe` returns a `String`, and `null` fills the gap
choices.why: A switch expression has no gap to fill; it must produce a value for every input.

prompt: `Os Sertões` (640 pages) printed `a long book`, while `Dom Casmurro` (256) printed its page count. Why?
hint: Cases are tried from the top.

choices.text: Because the unguarded `Book` case is skipped for books over 500 pages
choices.why: It is not skipped; the guarded case simply matched first.

choices.text: The guarded case comes first and only the 640-page book passes `pages > 500`
choices.why: Right: the other book fell through to the unguarded `Book` case.

choices.text: Because `when` sorts the books by page count
choices.why: `when` is a condition on one case; it sorts nothing.

prompt: Fill in the keyword that adds a guard: `case Book(String t, int p) ___ p > 500 -> ...`
hint: Section 04 used it on the long books.

prompt: `record Loan(String isbn, String member) { private String dueDate; }` does not compile. What does the error say, and why?
hint: `equals` and `toString` are built from the header.

choices.text: That `dueDate` must be `final`
choices.why: The message asked for `static`, and offered a component instead.

choices.text: That a field must be static: state outside the header would hide from `equals`
choices.why: Right: a record's instance state is its components and nothing else.

choices.text: That records cannot hold dates
choices.why: Any type can be a component; the problem is where the field was declared.

prompt: A library loan is renewed: same book, same member, a new due date. Why does the section make it a class rather than a record?
hint: Is it the same loan after the renewal?

choices.text: Because a record cannot hold a `LocalDate`
choices.why: It can; `record Loan(String isbn, String member, LocalDate dueDate)` compiles.

choices.text: Because records are slower than classes
choices.why: Speed is not the argument; identity is.

choices.text: It keeps one identity while its values change, and equal records count as one thing
choices.why: Right: two loans with equal fields would be `equals`, yet they are different loans.

choices.text: Because a record would need a setter for the date
choices.why: A record cannot have one; but the reason to choose a class is identity, not the missing setter.

prompt: Match each thing to the better choice for it.
hint: Are two with equal fields the same thing?

pairs.left: a member's account, whose balance changes

prompt: `record Point(int x, int y)` and `p.x = 3;` — what happens?
hint: What kind of field is `x`?

choices.text: It compiles, and `p` now has `x` equal to 3
choices.why: The field is private and final; neither the access nor the assignment is allowed.

choices.text: It does not compile
choices.why: Right: the field is `private final`. The way to a point with another `x` is `new Point(3, p.y())`.

choices.text: It compiles and throws `UnsupportedOperationException` when it runs
choices.why: That exception came from a list in section 03; a field assignment is checked at compile time.

prompt: Put what happens in `new Isbn(" 978-85-359-0277-1 ")` in order.
hint: The field is assigned last.
items: The canonical constructor is called with the string
The compact block removes the hyphens and the spaces from the parameter
The block checks that thirteen characters are left
The field `value` is assigned from the parameter

prompt: Which of these may a record declare? Choose all that apply.
hint: Section 05 listed what is allowed and what is not.

choices.text: An instance method, such as `boolean isLong()`
choices.why: Yes: methods are allowed; only extra instance state is not.

choices.text: A static field
choices.why: Yes: the error message asked for exactly that.

choices.text: `implements Item`
choices.why: Yes: section 04's records implemented a sealed interface.

choices.text: `extends Item`, when `Item` is a class
choices.why: No: a record already extends `java.lang.Record`.
